Description:
Ships: every transaction carries an authentication outcome; step-downs classified incident vs pattern-suspicious. Dark — no merchant-facing change.

Requirements: REQ-D1, REQ-D2

Depends on: —

Test harness:
- Timeout injection: force an auth timeout; assert stepped-down recorded before authorization proceeds
- Path audit: static check that no branch reaches authorization without an outcome write
- Classification: seeded incident cluster and seeded merchant-concentrated series label correctly

Summary: REQ-D1 · Record an authentication outcome on every transaction
Description:
Every transaction records exactly one authentication outcome — completed, attempted, stepped-down, or not-attempted — with a reason code and timestamp, written before authorization proceeds.

Source: PR ¶3 / IFAQ-07

Provenance: [OBSERVED] × 2

Out of scope: showing the field to merchants (REQ-DP1)

Depends on: —
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN a transaction whose authentication call exceeds the timeout
WHEN  the gateway continues processing on any path
THEN  an outcome of stepped-down with reason auth-timeout is recorded before the authorization is sent
AND   no code path reaches authorization with no outcome recorded

Summary: REQ-D2 · Distinguish incident timeouts from suspicious timeout patterns
Description:
Step-down events are classifiable as provider-incident (clustered, provider-wide) or pattern-suspicious (concentrated by merchant, card range, or timing), and the classification is recorded.

Source: 03-demo-spec.md F2 / IFAQ-03

Provenance: [OBSERVED] × 1, [UNKNOWN] × 1

Out of scope: acting on the classification (BLK-03 unresolved)

Depends on: REQ-D1, BLK-03
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN a window containing a provider-wide timeout cluster and an unrelated single-merchant timeout series
WHEN  classification runs
THEN  the cluster is labelled provider-incident and the series is labelled pattern-suspicious
AND   pattern-suspicious events are flagged for review, not auto-blocked

Description:
Ships: outcome field in reporting and API; same-day digest with incident grouping.

Requirements: REQ-DP1, REQ-DP2

Depends on: R1

Test harness:
- Field parity: recorded event and API/reporting field match on all four outcomes
- Digest grouping: 400 incident step-downs render one line; 3 unrelated render three rows
- Visibility lag under 24h on seeded events (M3)

Summary: REQ-DP1 · Expose the authentication outcome to merchants
Description:
The authentication outcome, reason, and timestamp appear on the transaction record in reporting and the API for every transaction from launch.

Source: PR ¶3 / EFAQ-02

Provenance: [OBSERVED] × 2

Out of scope: historical backfill (REQ-D3)

Depends on: REQ-D1
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN a transaction with outcome stepped-down
WHEN  the merchant retrieves it via reporting or API
THEN  the outcome, reason and timestamp are present and match the recorded event

Description:
Merchants with at least one step-down in a day receive a digest within 24 hours, with provider incidents grouped into a single line.

Source: PR ¶3 / 03-demo-spec.md F2

Provenance: [OBSERVED] × 1

Out of scope: real-time webhooks; alert thresholds

Depends on: REQ-D1, REQ-D2
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN 400 step-downs caused by one provider incident and 3 unrelated ones
WHEN  the digest is generated
THEN  it shows one incident line covering the 400 and three individual rows

Description:
Ships: policy control with allow/block live for all merchants; require-exemption if BLK-02 permits; no silent path anywhere.

Requirements: REQ-DP3, REQ-DP5, REQ-DP4

Depends on: R2

Blocked by: BLK-02, BLK-06

Test harness:
- Policy block: timeout produces authentication-unavailable decline, outcome attempted
- Policy-service failure: outcome stepped-down / policy-unavailable, never silent, never completed
- Distinct decline reason survives acquirer response-code mapping (Q-07)

Merchants can set on-timeout policy to allow or block; the gateway consults it before any unauthenticated retry on every path; default is allow.

Source: PR ¶5 / EFAQ-04

Provenance: [OBSERVED] × 1

Out of scope: the require-exemption option (REQ-DP4)

Depends on: REQ-D1
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN a merchant with policy block
WHEN  an authentication call times out
THEN  the payment fails with decline reason authentication-unavailable and outcome attempted
AND   with policy allow, the transaction proceeds and records stepped-down

Description:
No code path processes a transaction unauthenticated without a recorded outcome and a policy consultation; failure of the policy service itself records policy-unavailable.

Source: PR ¶1 / 03-demo-spec.md F4

Provenance: [OBSERVED] × 1

Out of scope: changing the default policy under failure

Depends on: REQ-D1, REQ-DP3
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN the policy service is unreachable
WHEN  an authentication call times out
THEN  the transaction records stepped-down with reason policy-unavailable
AND   a code-path audit shows no branch reaching authorization without a recorded outcome

Summary: REQ-DP4 · Exemption-flagged step-down for EEA transactions
Description:
Where a compliance determination permits it, stepped-down EEA transactions carry the determined exemption flag.

Source: RFAQ-02 / PR ¶5

Provenance: [OBSERVED] × 1, [UNKNOWN] × 1

Out of scope: jurisdictions where step-down is not offerable (Q-12)

Depends on: BLK-02, REQ-DP3

Conditional on: BLK-02 — which exemption, whether any applies, and whether the option exists at all are compliance determinations not made here
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN the compliance determination names an applicable exemption
WHEN  a step-down occurs on an in-scope transaction under policy require-exemption
THEN  the transaction carries that exemption flag and records it in the outcome reason

Description:
Ships: historical enumeration joined to chargebacks; the measured fraud differential (M6); the evidentiary input to any restitution decision.

Requirements: REQ-D3, REQ-D4

Depends on: R1

Blocked by: BLK-01, BLK-05

Test harness:
- Join over seeded history returns chargeback outcomes per stepped-down transaction
- Ranges predating retention state so explicitly
- M6 report includes populations and period; refutation path for C5 recorded

Summary: REQ-D3 · Enumerate historical step-downs and join to chargebacks
Description:
For the retained log window, produce per-merchant step-down counts joined to fraud chargebacks on those transactions.

Source: EFAQ-05 / IFAQ-07

Provenance: [OBSERVED] × 1, [UNKNOWN] × 1

Out of scope: any restitution decision (BLK-01)

Depends on: BLK-05

Conditional on: BLK-05 — if join keys do not survive, this becomes counts-only, and REQ-DP6 (restitution input) loses its evidentiary basis
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN the retained auth event log and chargeback records
WHEN  the join is computed for a merchant and date range
THEN  the output lists stepped-down transactions and their chargeback outcomes, or states that the range predates retained data

Summary: REQ-D4 · Measure the fraud differential on stepped-down transactions
Description:
Report chargeback rate on stepped-down versus authenticated transactions over a comparable period (metric M6).

Source: PR ¶2 / IFAQ-04

Provenance: [ASSUMED] × 1 → RESTS ON ASSUMPTION

Out of scope: causal attribution

Depends on: REQ-D3
Acceptance Criteria:
GIVEN the chargeback join exists for a full quarter
WHEN  M6 is computed
THEN  the report states both rates, the population sizes, and the period
AND   if the differential is not significant, claim C5 is marked refuted in the session record
